facts.statement: Charles William Andrews described the type species Sarcosaurus woodi in 1921 based on a partial skeleton found by S.L. Wood near Barrow-on-Soar.
facts.quote: The type species, Sarcosaurus woodi, was first described by Charles William Andrews in 1921 shortly after a partial skeleton had been found by S.L. Wood near Barrow-on-Soar, in the Scunthorpe Mudstone.

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus lived in what is now England, Ireland, and Scotland during the Early Jurassic, approximately 199 to 196 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived in what is now England and maybe Ireland and Scotland during the Hettangian-Sinemurian stages of the Early Jurassic, about 199-196 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Sarcosaurus was a 3.5-meter-long animal weighing no more than 50 to 60 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype belonged to a 3.5-metre-long animal whose weight was no greater than 50–60 kg.

facts.statement: A referred specimen, NHMUK PV R3542, belonged to a larger individual estimated to reach 5 meters in length and weigh 140 kilograms.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R3542 belonged to a larger animal, estimated to have had a maximum length of 5 m and a weight of 140 kg.

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus was a bipedal predator capable of running fast to catch small prey.
facts.quote: Sarcosaurus was a bipedal predator, probably able to run fast and catch small prey.

facts.statement: Three fossils were discovered between 1980 and 2000 on a beach near The Gobbins in Northern Ireland by paleontologist Roger Byrne.
facts.quote: Between the years 1980 and 2000, three fossils were discovered on a beach near The Gobbins in Northern Ireland by palaeontologist Roger Byrne.

facts.statement: The theropod tibia found in Northern Ireland is one of the only known dinosaur remains from the island, which has a poor Mesozoic fossil record.
facts.quote: The indeterminate dinosaur femur and theropod tibia are the only known remains of dinosaurs from Ireland, which has a poor Mesozoic fossil record entirely consisting of marine localities, and the indeterminate dinosaur specimen was the first ever reported from the island.

facts.statement: In 2020, Ezcurra et al. classified Sarcosaurus as a close relative of Averostra based on shared skeletal characters.
facts.quote: In 2020, Ezcurra et al. recovered Sarcosaurus as a close relative of Averostra due to the presence of shared characters including an anteroventrally oriented ventral margin of the preacetabular process in lateral view on the ilium and a femur with a poorly posteriorly developed fourth trochanter.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the two named species of Sarcosaurus are distinct, with some authors considering them indistinguishable and others labeling them as nomina dubia due to a lack of unique features.
facts.quote: A later study concluded the two species to be indistinguishable except for size, but other authors consider any identity to be unprovable as there are no comparable remains and conclude both species to lack autapomorphies and therefore to be nomina dubia.

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus fossils were found in strata deposited in shallow, marine settings with a warm and humid climate.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was collected from strata (bucklandi zone, Sinemurian) that were deposited in epicontinental, shallow, marine settings affected by sea-level fluctuations and a warm, predominantly humid climate.

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus is classified within the superfamily Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Coelophysoidea

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus woodi is the only known species of the extinct genus Sarcosaurus.
facts.quote: Sarcosaurus woodi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Sarcosaurus

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus lived during the early Jurassic, approximately 199 to 194 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 199 a 194 millones de años

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus lived in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Europa

facts.statement: The type species Sarcosaurus woodi was described by Andrews in 1921.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, S. woodi, fue descripta por Andrews en 1921

facts.statement: Remains of Sarcosaurus include a partial skeleton found in England.
facts.quote: Los restos de Sarcosaurus incluyen un esqueleto parcial, encontrado en Inglaterra

facts.statement: The remains were found in the Lower Lias of Leicestershire and Warwickshire.
facts.quote: en los bajos Lias de Leicestershre y Warwickshire

facts.statement: The generic name Sarcosaurus is derived from the Greek word sarx, meaning "flesh" or "meat".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego sarx, "carne"

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus woodi was first described by Charles William Andrews in 1921 after S. L. Wood found a partial skeleton near Barrow-on-Soar in Scunthorpe Mudstone.
facts.quote: Sarcosaurus woodi, fue descrita por primera vez por Charles William Andrews en 1921 poco después de que S. L. Wood encontrara un esqueleto parcial cerca de Barrow-on-Soar, en Scunthorpe Mudstone

facts.statement: Sarcosaurus was a bipedal predator, likely capable of running fast and catching small prey.
facts.quote: Sarcosaurus era un depredador bípedo, probablemente capaz de correr rápido y atrapar presas pequeñas

facts.statement: The holotype belonged to an animal 3.5 meters long with a weight not exceeding 50-60 kilograms.
facts.quote: El holotipo pertenecía a un animal de 3,5 metros de largo cuyo peso no superaba los 50-60 kilogramos

facts.statement: Specimen NHMUK PV R3542 belonged to a larger animal estimated to have a maximum length of 5 meters and a weight of 140 kilograms.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R3542 pertenecía a un animal más grande, que se estima que tenía una longitud máxima de 5 metros y un peso de 140 kilogramos

facts.statement: A second species, Sarcosaurus andrewsi, was named by Friedrich von Huene in 1932 based on a 445-millimeter tibia.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, Sarcosaurus andrewsi, fue nombrada por Friedrich von Huene en 1932, basándose en una tibia de 445 milímetros

facts.statement: Confusingly, von Huene named the same fossil Magnosaurus woodwardi in the same publication.
facts.quote: De manera confusa, von Huene en la misma publicación nombró al mismo fósil Magnosaurus woodwardi

facts.statement: In 2020, a complete new description proposed that three specimens belonged to the same species, Sarcosaurus woodi.
facts.quote: En 2020, WARMS G667–690 recibió una nueva descripción completa, que proponía que los tres especímenes pertenecían a la misma especie, Sarcosaurus woodi

facts.statement: Andrews originally assigned Sarcosaurus to the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Andrews originalmente asignó Sarcosaurus a Megalosauridae

facts.statement: Later analyses resulted in a position for Sarcosaurus in Ceratosauria or Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: Análisis posteriores dieron como resultado una posición en Ceratosauria, o en Coelophysoidea

facts.statement: In 2018, Andrea Cau found Sarcosaurus to be a dilophosaurid with strong data support in a major analysis.
facts.quote: En 2018, Andrea Cau en el gran análisis de Saltriovenator encontró a Sarcosaurus como un dilofosáurido con una buena cantidad de apoyo en los datos

facts.statement: In 2020, Ezcurra et al. recovered Sarcosaurus as a close relative of Averostra.
facts.quote: En 2020, Ezcurra et al. recuperó Sarcosaurus como un pariente cercano de Averostra

facts.statement: The parent group of Sarcosaurus is Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysoidea

facts.statement: The time range for Sarcosaurus is from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from Sinemurian strata deposited in shallow epicontinental marine environments with warm, predominantly humid climates.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo fue recolectado de estratos de la zona bucklandi, del Sinemuriense, que fueron depositados en ambientes marinos epicontinentales, poco profundos, afectados por fluctuaciones del nivel del mar y un clima cálido, predominantemente húmedo

facts.statement: The Rugby limestone member was deposited at a paleolatitude of approximately 35° N in a storm-influenced coastal environment.
facts.quote: El miembro de piedra caliza Rugby se depositó en una paleolatitude de aproximadamente 35° N en un entorno costero influenciado por tormentas

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sarcosaurus andrewsi is a valid species; some studies find it indistinguishable from S. woodi except by size, while others consider both species doubtful due to a lack of comparable remains and autapomorphies.
facts.quote: Un estudio posterior concluyó que las dos especies son indistinguibles excepto por el tamaño, pero otros autores consideran que cualquier identidad es indemostrable ya que no hay restos comparables y concluyen que ambas especies carecen de autapomorfias y, por lo tanto, son dudosas
